---
title: "On-going User"
---

> There are a few ways to navigate GitHub for on-going use:
>
> 1.  Create a new repository through [GitHub](github.com) – creating a new repository on the cloud
> 2.  Clone a repository through GitHub Desktop – adding a repository that’s on the cloud onto your local computer
> 3.  Create a new repository through GitHub Desktop – creating a new repository onto your local computer
> 4.  Add an existing R project as new repository

# 1. Create a new repository on [GitHub](github.com)

-   Go to [GitHub](github.com) and make sure you're logged in

-   Near "Repositories", click [**New**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button

-   How to fill this in:

    -   Repository template: [No template]{style="color:red; "}

    -   Repository name: [desired repository name]{style="color:red; "}

    -   Description: [any information you want fellow users to know]{style="color:red; "}

    -   **Private**

    -   Initialize this repository with: **Add a README file**

-   Click [**Create repository**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button

-   Click [**\<\>Code**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button

-   Copy the HTTPS address

# 2. Clone a repository through GitHub Desktop

-   Click **Current repository** ▼

-   Click **Add** ▼

-   Click **Clone a repository...**

Now, there are 2 choices... you can either a) search through the existing repositories b) copy and paste the HTTPS address

a.  In the **GitHub.com** tab:

    -   select the existing repository

    -   choose local path you'd like to save it to

b.  In the **URL** tab:

    -   select the existing repository

    -   choose local path you'd like to save it to

-   Click [**Clone**]{style="color:#99CCFF;font-weight:bold;"}

# 3. Create a new repository through GitHub Desktop

-   Click **Current repository** ▼

-   Click **Add** ▼

-   Click **Create a new repository..**

<!-- -->

-   How to fill this in:

    -   Repository name: [desired repository name]{style="color:red; "}

    -   Description: [any information you want fellow users to know]{style="color:red; "}

    -   Local path: choose path you'd like to save it to

    -   ![](images/clipboard-33796902.png)Initialize this repository with a **README**

    -   Git ignore: ▼ scroll and select **R**

    -   License: None

    -   Click [**Create repository**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button

It will ask if you want to Publish repository, click [**Publish repository**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button

# 4. Add an existing R project as a new repository

-   Open your .Rproj file

-   At the top of your RStudio window, click “**Tools**”

-   Click “**Version Control \> Project setup…**”

-   A new window “**Project Options**” window will open with “**Git/SVN**”tab displayed

    -   Change Version control systems (None)▼ to **Git**

A pop up message:

> Confirm Restart RStudio
>
> You’ll need to restart RStudio in order for this change to take effect. Do you want to do this now?

Click “**Yes**”

-   Go to GitHub Desktop

-   Click **Current repository** ▼

-   At the bottom under **Other**, you'll notice your project - click it

It will ask if you want to Publish repository - click [**Publish repository**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button

-   How to fill this in:

    -   Repository name: [desired repository name]{style="color:red; "}

    -   Description: [any information you want fellow users to know]{style="color:red; "}

    -   ![](images/clipboard-33796902.png)Keep this code private

    -   Click [**Create repository**]{style="color:#33CC33;font-weight:bold;"} button
